policy: Upstream owns shared capabilities; retain missing behavior using small integration points. No isolation implementation. Preserve upstream membership persistence and Hermes provider/plugin/parser.

upstream_owned.note: Run conformance on pristine upstream first. No legacy Hermes backend/plugin/spec/parser port.

transcript-path-diagnostic.behavior: Missing executable with inaccessible PATH, real nonexecutable candidate and explicit paths have distinct diagnostics. No missing tool becomes an empty successful result.
transcript-path-diagnostic.upstream_difference: Fork distinguishes inaccessible PATH directories from a real non-executable candidate/explicit path; upstream run_search_tool has only NotFound vs general spawn error.

recent-kimi-bind-safety.behavior: Competing connection lock, old session-binding removal, canonical primary repair, foreign ownership rejection and historical SessionEnd safety.
recent-kimi-bind-safety.upstream_difference: Upstream has immediate transaction/tool-owner checks; fork additionally repairs Kimi primary session and purges stale aliases in bind_session_to_process_for_tool.

behavior: Two explicit direct hcom starts in one Claude native session converge on one existing binding and do not mint a second row.
Without the explicit native-participation opt-in, a direct no-process Claude hook remains silent and does not claim a pending row.
If native participation is opted in, its session export/handshake is scoped to that authoritative opt-in and cannot by itself claim an unrelated pending row.
An hcom-launched Claude still binds and validates through the upstream process path.
If Claude-tagged vanilla participation is selected later, add an explicit product test for its ownership and cross-tool constraints instead of reviving the old fallback implicitly.
claude-native-session-start-adoption.upstream_difference: Fork explicit native hook opt-in plus session-keyed direct start; upstream native delivery refers to launched-agent transport, not this participation path.

behavior: A VS Code SessionStart with no HCOM_PROCESS_ID creates one codex row and a session binding using the supplied transcript/cwd.
A repeated or concurrent SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit for that session returns the same row and never creates a duplicate.
The first ordinary UserPromptSubmit can deliver pending hcom context after adoption.
Wrong originator, missing session, SessionEnd, tool hooks, and stop hooks do not create identities or bypass the gate.
A failed transaction leaves no partially created row or session binding.
codex-wrapperless-vscode-adoption.upstream_difference: Fork narrowly enrolls codex_vscode SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit without launch process ID; upstream resolves launched process binding.

behavior: A no-process command with a previously bound Codex thread resolves the same sender and session ID.
An unknown thread returns identity-required and creates no row.
Explicit session/name and process binding retain precedence over the thread lookup.
A thread bound to a non-Codex row is rejected or ignored rather than attributed to Codex.
No transcript text or marker is consulted by command identity resolution.
codex-thread-sender-resolution.upstream_difference: Fork permits read-only lookup of an already Codex-owned session through CODEX_THREAD_ID without HCOM_PROCESS_ID; upstream lacks that final identity fallback.

behavior: A process/session/stopped owner of another tool returns Rejected and leaves every binding and placeholder mutation unchanged.
A same-tool existing owner remains idempotent and a permitted unbound case creates the expected row only when create_if_unbound is true.
Claude generation attach preserves a live foreign process binding and removes only a stale conflict.
Wrapperless Codex adoption cannot overwrite a Claude, Kimi, Qoder, or stopped foreign row keyed by the same native ID.
Database failure rolls back both binding and any attempted orphan creation.
tool-family-authoritative-binding.upstream_difference: Checked binder exists upstream; fork extends its use into native Codex/Hermes callers and enrollment paths.

hermes-core-provider.behavior: Hermes Core Provider Integration & Spec Registration
hermes-core-provider.upstream_difference: Upstream provides this Hermes capability at feature level through its own implementation; this does not certify a drop-in replacement for every edge case.

hermes-tool-detection.behavior: Hermes Tool Detection Predicates & Child Environment Scrubbing
hermes-tool-detection.upstream_difference: Upstream provides this Hermes capability at feature level through its own implementation; this does not certify a drop-in replacement for every edge case.

hermes-session-attribution.behavior: Hermes Subprocess Identity Attribution & Read-Only Resolution
hermes-session-attribution.upstream_difference: Fork resolves ordinary terminal commands from an enrolled HERMES_SESSION_ID without process binding; upstream normal terminal plugin remains launch-gated.

hermes-hook-dispatch.behavior: Extend upstream Hermes Pi-family RPC only for guarded ordinary-terminal participation; preserve its plugin, gateway bridges and delivery acknowledgement protocol.
hermes-hook-dispatch.upstream_difference: Both have Hermes RPC/lifecycle handlers; fork adds ordinary-session/read-only resolution and checked ownership. Upstream adds shared Pi-family RPC and gateway paths.

hermes-session-adoption.behavior: Ordinary Session Adoption & Stopped Row Recovery
hermes-session-adoption.upstream_difference: Fork can adopt ordinary Hermes terminals without hcom launch and recover their session row; upstream normal terminal handle_start requires HCOM_PROCESS_ID (gateway bridges are separate).

hermes-backend-plugin.upstream_difference: Upstream provides this Hermes capability at feature level through its own implementation; this does not certify a drop-in replacement for every edge case.

hermes-backend-ownership.behavior: Hermes Plugin Ownership, Installation, and Readiness Evaluation
hermes-backend-ownership.upstream_difference: Upstream provides this Hermes capability at feature level through its own implementation; this does not certify a drop-in replacement for every edge case.

hermes-launch-resume-config.behavior: Hermes Launch Formatting, Resume Argument Merging, and Config
hermes-launch-resume-config.upstream_difference: Upstream provides this Hermes capability at feature level through its own implementation; this does not certify a drop-in replacement for every edge case.

hermes-bootstrap.upstream_difference: Upstream provides this Hermes capability at feature level through its own implementation; this does not certify a drop-in replacement for every edge case.

hermes-transcript.behavior: Hermes SQLite Transcript Parser & Multi-Profile Search
hermes-transcript.upstream_difference: SQLite transcript support exists upstream. Fork --all search additionally gathers recorded DBs from live and stopped Hermes rows across profiles; upstream database_search_path selects ambient profile.

behavior: After-id is exclusive and catches results preceding arm; default cursor observes future events
Unrelated inbox remains unread; no temporary subscription or synthetic notice
Final scan precedes timeout; JSON discriminates match/timeout; timeout exit1 unless --timeout-ok
Normal CLI/TUI masks internal markers; verbose retains diagnostic detail
Short listens never change persistent wait_timeout
filtered-listen-isolation.upstream_difference: Fork direct event query does not consume unrelated inbox messages or create synthetic subscription notices; upstream listen_filtered creates temp subscription and consumes InlineBatch inbox messages.

behavior: Filtered or explicit-cursor waits return only matching events
A prelaunch cursor catches an event before arm; no historical replay
Default snapshots and persistent subscription behavior remain unchanged
Filtered or explicit-cursor waits emit no unrelated preview; unfiltered waits retain upstream preview-once-and-continue behavior.

Without after-id, waits arm at the current durable cursor, including unfiltered waits; upstream's 10-second quick lookback is intentionally not retained. Capture a cursor before launching work to include events that precede the wait.
events-wait-boundaries.upstream_difference: Fork one-shot waits accept durable after-id and suppress unrelated previews for filtered/cursor waits; upstream --after-id is follow-only and wait prints unread preview. Default unfiltered wait also moves from upstream's 10-second lookback to cursor-at-arm semantics; its preview-once-and-continue behavior is retained.

behavior: Ordered flush after each record; resume no replay
Soft stop retains generation; exact terminal stop ends follow; reused name excluded
Broken pipe/signals cleanly exit and clean only this endpoint
No subscription, inbox, request-watch or worker-state mutations
durable-events-stream.upstream_difference: Both have ordered flushed event tails/cursor resume/broken-pipe handling. Fork stream --follow NAME pins exact worker generation and stops on its terminal end; upstream --follow is a generic boolean stream mode.

behavior: Typed schema and optional thread; no raw command/env/message/transcript fields
Hostile file detail excluded; accepted path-like text remains untrusted
Quiet heartbeats bounded; real phase transitions immediate
Independent request/reply remains functional while compact observer runs
compact-progress-stream.upstream_difference: Fork-only compact typed records, cadence coalescing and quiet heartbeat projection; no raw message/command/env fields in compact schema.

behavior: Reject ambiguous generation or conflicting filters; require one thread and durable attempt cursor
ACKs, other threads/workers and reused names cannot satisfy result
Pre-arm blockers found; cleared blockers ignored; final poll precedes deadline
Exit0 result,1 deadline,2 SQL,3 unavailable,4 blocker,5 launch failure; preserve recovery/correlation evidence
correlated-result-outcomes.upstream_difference: Fork --result-from pins worker generation/thread/attempt and returns typed result/deadline/SQL/unavailable/blocker/launch-failure outcomes. No counterpart in upstream EventsArgs.

behavior: Wrong session/thread, ambiguous or unsupported provider returns unavailable
Earlier resumed turn cannot replay as new result
Normal authored report takes precedence; recovery records provenance
provider-result-recovery.upstream_difference: Fork scoped stopped-generation transcript result recovery with provider/session/thread provenance; upstream has no corresponding result-wait subsystem.

behavior: Ordinary text mentioning trust is not a blocker
Actual trust/approval/quota/auth states retain correct kind and evidence
Resolved blockers cannot terminate a later wait; recovery cannot clear an outstanding provider approval
typed-launch-blockers.upstream_difference: Both report launch blockage. Fork additionally classifies auth/quota/trust/etc as structured blocker records and integrates them with correlated waits.

behavior: Targeted messages seed thread delivery membership; recipient-free followups address known members.
Thread-resolved requests receive request-watch coverage.
Preserve upstream membership/subscription persistence across stop/resume and ownership guards; do not restore the older downstream stop-cleanup policy.
thread-membership-lifetime.upstream_difference: Thread routing, stop/resume membership and subscription persistence stay upstream-owned. Retained delta adds request-watch coverage for thread-resolved requests; older downstream stop-cleanup policy is intentionally dropped.

behavior: Correct ACK does not close completion watch; later inform does
Nested request is not a completion
Absent/empty legacy intent stays inform; ACK never required
request-ack-result-separation.upstream_difference: Fork only inform/legacy intent completes a request watch; upstream cancellation paths receive no intent and may cancel on ACK or nested request.

behavior: No accidental implicit global send
Exact bare target accepted; ambiguous input gives canonical syntax before stdin
--broadcast rejects explicit targets/thread conflict
Seeded thread followup remains recipient-free without global fanout
explicit-send-policy.upstream_difference: Fork requires explicit --broadcast for global fanout and validates target/thread conflicts; upstream accepts recipient-free text broadcasts with preview/ambiguity handling.

behavior: Only actual targeted/thread recipients wake
Explicit broadcast still wakes all
No endpoint remains harmless; unrelated event subscribers still get relevant wake
targeted-recipient-wake.upstream_difference: Fork wakes resolved recipients for targeted/thread sends; upstream send_message calls wake_all.

behavior: Sibling PostToolUse/failure/denial leaves owning approval blocked
Owner completion/denial resolves it; replaced approval survives stale token
Late approval survives nonapproval restore; DB errors fail closed
PTY falling edge does not clear a different replacement approval
approval-owner-race-safety.upstream_difference: Fork tracks pending approval owner/tool-use token and rejects stale/sibling clears; upstream has general delivery gate race guards but PostToolUse clears a blocked row without this owner token protocol.

behavior: Concurrent manual start/hook ACK emits exactly one connected event
Failed transaction emits neither claim nor event
Bootstrap write/ACK contract remains intact
TUI and filters recognize connection as startup activity
subagent-connected-signal.upstream_difference: Fork emits one atomic durable life.connected event on actual bootstrap/start ACK; upstream has no corresponding life event path.

behavior: Known accept-edits, plan and best-of-N composer mode banners, including narrow-pane wraps, represent an empty prompt even when not dim-styled.
Real typed input remains protected; delivery follows existing inject/verify/submit gates and submit-edge tracking.
antigravity-idle-mode-banner.upstream_difference: Fork treats exact/wrapped known non-dim mode placeholders as empty prompt; upstream extractor relies on dim styling/readiness without banner recognition.

behavior: Recognize a complete active non-task survey, reject quotes/partial frames/real prompts and approval dialogs; Skip uses only byte0, never Enter.
Bounded stable-frame retries, redraw grace and wall-clock escalation publish pty:survey after failed dismissal; publication and release preserve foreign blocker ownership.
Unix and Windows share the same controller; row and status event changes commit atomically before notifications.
antigravity-feedback-survey.upstream_difference: Fork recognizes complete active survey and performs bounded Skip-only dismissal/typed fallback preserving blocker ownership. No corresponding upstream survey controller.
